<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 88:6">Targ. Ps. LXXXVIII, 6</cite>; a. fr.—
Sabb. 12ᵇ רחמנא יִדְכְּרִינָךְ וכ׳ the Lord remember thee for health.—Part. דְּכָר, דָּכְרָא, pass. דְּכִיר, דְּכִירָא remembering, reminded.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 137:1">Targ. Ps. CXXXVII, 1</cite> <he>הוינא דָכְרִין</he> (ed. Lag. <he>דְּכִירִין</he>).
Targ. Gen. VIII, 1; a. fr.; v. דְּכִיר.—2) to mention, remind.
Targ. Gen. XL, 14 (with על).—[Targ. Y. I Num. XXIV, 1, v. Af.].—
<cite ref="Shabbat 57a:6">Sabb. 57ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>מאן ד׳ שמיה</he> who mentioned his (its) name, i.e. what has this to do here?
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Numbers 24:1">Targ. Y. II, Num. XXIV, 1</cite> (Y. I <he>מִד׳</he>, corr. acc.); a. e.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 31a">Ber. 31ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>אַדְכַּרְתָּן מילתא וכ׳</he> thou recallest to my mind what R. … said; <cite ref="Sukkah 53a">Succ. 53ᵃ</cite> bot.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 82a:2">Snh. 82ᵃ</cite> <he>אַדְכְּרֵיה רב לגמריה</he> (by reciting the verse) he recalled to Rabs’ mind a tradition, v. <cite ref="C01067"><he>גְּמָרָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Niddah 24b:45">Nidd. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>דכי מַדְכְּרוּ ליה מִדְּכַר</he> that when they mention it (the reason), one should be reminded (that he has heard the law before).
<cite ref="Ketubot 20a:9">Keth. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>מַדְכַּר חד לחבריה</he> one (witness) may recall (the circumstances) to the other’s mind.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 11:19">Targ. Jer. XI, 19</cite> <he>יִדְּכַר</he> (not <he>יִדְכַּר</he>).
